subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this broad cron session accumulation issue remain the umbrella while the retention and cadence guardrail PRs are decided, or should the remaining work be split into narrower canonical items now?
rationale: Current main still has a real retention bug, but the warning and cadence-limit portions change operator-facing cron policy and overlap active maintainer-reviewed PRs.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Open
options.body: Keep this issue open until the retention and cadence PRs are landed, replaced, or rejected, then triage any leftover context-warning scope.

options.title: Split Remaining Scope
options.body: Make the isolated base-session retention report the canonical bug and open a separate maintainer-owned item for context-pressure warnings or cadence policy.

options.title: Close After Slice Decisions
options.body: Close this issue only after the active slice decisions are recorded and no untracked guardrail behavior remains.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Open
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the retention and cadence PRs are landed, replaced, or rejected, then triage any leftover context-warning scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent current-main localization of the cron/session reaper code involved in this review and can route the retention slice against the active PRs.
